_about: Presolv360 dispute clause rating scale. Source of truth: Presolv360's clause rating document and a set of reference agreements, with mixed-clause averaging ruled by the legal team on 2026-11-03. Signals are regular expressions matched against the clause in lowercase, with line breaks and extra spaces collapsed to single spaces. 'risk' is the one-line reason shown on the card; 'strengths' are the key takeaways shown for good ratings (4/5 and above).

types.label: Presolv360
types.headline: A named online institution runs the case and picks the arbitrator.
types.risk: A named, neutral online institution appoints the arbitrator under its own rules, which leaves little room to dispute the appointment and lets the case move quickly.
strengths: A named, independent institution appoints the arbitrator, so neither side picks the judge.
The institution's own rules govern the process, which reduces arguments about procedure.
The case can run online, so filings and hearings need no travel.
types.meaning: Presolv360 is named in the contract as the institution that administers the arbitration (alone or as one of the named options), and the arbitrator is appointed under its rules.

types.label: ODR
types.headline: An online institution picks the arbitrator, but none is named in the contract.
types.risk: An online institution rather than the lender appoints the arbitrator, which keeps the process neutral, but because none is named the parties may argue over which one to use.
strengths: An online dispute resolution institution, not the lender, appoints the arbitrator.
The institution's rules govern the process, which keeps the procedure neutral.
The case can run online, which keeps it quick and low-cost.
types.meaning: An online dispute resolution institution appoints the arbitrator under its rules, but no institution is named in the contract (for example, any ODR on a list kept by the lender).
signals: appointed by any online dispute resolution
administered electronically under online dispute resolution

types.label: Institutional
types.headline: An institution picks the arbitrator, but it is not named.
types.risk: An institution appoints the arbitrator, but because it is only described and not named, the parties can dispute which institution qualifies, which can delay the start of the case.
types.meaning: An unnamed institution (for example 'a recognised independent institution' or 'an institution recognized by the government of India') administers the arbitration and appoints the arbitrator.

types.label: Mutual consent
types.headline: Both sides must agree on the arbitrator, which can stall the case.
types.risk: Both sides must agree on one arbitrator, so if they cannot agree, or the borrower must pick from names the lender chose, a party may have to go to court for an appointment, causing delay.
types.meaning: The parties appoint the sole arbitrator by mutual consent, including when the borrower must choose from names proposed by the lender.

types.label: Unilateral
types.headline: The lender picks the judge for its own case.
types.risk: The lender alone picks the arbitrator, so the appointment can be challenged as one-sided, risking court applications, delay and the award being set aside.
types.meaning: The lender alone nominates or appoints the arbitrator.

mixed_clause_rules: If the clause has more than one way of picking the arbitrator, the rating is the average of the ratings of each way, shown to one decimal place (example: Unilateral 2/5 + ODR 4/5 = 3/5). A 'notwithstanding' part does not override the rest. Ruled by the legal team on 2026-11-03.
Presolv360 named together with other named ODR institutions only is one way of picking, rated 5/5. Presolv360 together with 'any other ODR platform' is a mix of Presolv360 5/5 and ODR 4/5, so 4.5/5.
Rate by who picks the arbitrator. Wording that only says the case may be conducted online does not change the rating (a mutual consent clause with online hearings stays 3/5).

mixed.label: Mixed
mixed.headline: This clause has more than one way of picking the arbitrator, so the rating is the average of its parts.
mixed.risk: It is not clear which way of picking the arbitrator applies, which invites an argument when a dispute arises.
mixed.recommendation: Keep the clause straightforward and unambiguous: use a single way of picking the arbitrator. Today it mentions {labels}.
